about: Pontet-Canet, a Fifth Growth of 1855, is named for Jean-François de Pontet, an 18th-century royal governor of the Médoc, and the Canet lands his family added. The Cruse family of Bordeaux merchants owned it from 1865 for 110 years. Guy Tesseron, from a Cognac family, bought it in 1975, and his son Alfred took charge in 1994. Under the Tesserons the estate rose in quality and reputation, and many now place it alongside the Second Growths. Its 81 hectares of vines lie next to Mouton Rothschild.

The vineyard sits on deep gravel over clay and limestone and is planted mostly to Cabernet Sauvignon, with Merlot and small amounts of Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot. The 2005 came right after the estate began biodynamic trials in 2004 and before its full conversion and organic certification in 2010. It was aged in French oak, with more new oak and extraction than the château uses today, as Antonio Galloni of Vinous has noted.

2005 is one of the great Bordeaux vintages, and Pontet-Canet’s 2005 was built to last. Robert Parker called it possibly the youngest 2005 Médoc in its evolution, full-bodied and fresh with blueberry, blackberry and cassis. Two decades on, critics find blackcurrant, cedar, graphite and tobacco, with dense tannins and a saline, pencil-lead finish. Vinous gave it 96 points in 2021.
facts: Cabernet Sauvignon-led, with Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Petit Verdot
